| Field | Value |

## Problem

Your AI/ML signal work needs the SDR substrate — GNU Radio's DSP
pipeline feeding model-training corpora, signal capture for
audio/voice-model research — but no default image carries it: the C-7
rows are excluded from every ISO by construction because a multi-gig
DSP stack has no business inside a ≤4 GB budget. You want the pack on
ONE host, deliberately, and you want to verify exactly what landed.

## Solution

Confirm the rows, opt in via the pack derivation, rebuild, verify:

```bash
# 1. See the C-7 rows the manifest declares (all status: data)
kailash info gnuradio      # software-defined radio DSP framework (software-only)
kailash info gqrx          # SDR receiver built on GNU Radio
kailash info hackrf-tools  # CLI utilities for HackRF hardware SDR platforms
kailash list --category c-07-signal-sdr
#    -> the opt-in six: gnuradio, gqrx, hackrf-tools, sox, librosa, pysox

# 2. Opt in via the pack derivation in your host configuration — a
#    deliberate config act, NOT a category enablement:
#    environment.systemPackages = [ kailash-data.sdr-tools ];
#    (packs ride kailash-data.* opt-in gating at the OS side; they never
#     ride a default profile)

# 3. Rebuild and switch
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 4. Verify what landed, software side first (no hardware needed)
gnuradio-config-info --version
grcc --version 2>/dev/null || echo "grcc present: $(command -v grcc)"
hackrf_info 2>/dev/null || echo "no HackRF attached — CLI present, device probe: PENDING"
gqrx 2>&1 | head -2 || true   # GUI starts (or reports missing display in a headless shell)
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
pack:    c-07-signal-sdr    (kailash-data.sdr-tools, opt-in DATA pack)
version: <nvfetcher rev>    (the lock/sources revision)
status:  data pack installed, default-OFF pack opted in
gnuradio-config-info --version
3.x.x
hackrf_info
Found HackRF...            # when hardware is attached
No HackRF boards found.    # when none is — the CLI is present either way
```

What success looks like:

- the pack derivations are in the new system closure and the rebuild's
  diff-closures shows ONLY the pack's content (a category of attack or
  ops tooling snuck in is wrong — check what you actually declared)
- `gnuradio-config-info --version` answers (software-only, works
  without any radio hardware)
- `hackrf_info` runs; on a box WITH a HackRF it probes the device, on a
  box without it reports none found — the DSP-side research needs no RF
  hardware at all
- a rebuild WITHOUT the opt-in line removes the pack entirely — the
  opt-out is the same declarative act in reverse

## Discussion

- **Why SDR is a carve-out at all:** Kailash deliberately is NOT
  Kali-for-networks — wifi/RF/Bluetooth attack tooling does not ship.
  SDR is the one exception, and the reason is stated in the spec: SDR
  is the substrate for AI/ML signal research — radio-based ML datasets,
  signal-capture corpora for audio/voice-model work, GNURadio's DSP
  ecosystem feeding ML pipelines. The A-6 multi-modal attack surface
  (e.g. the pre-#210 voice-clone row — aspirational-only, removed; os#210 registry) needs software DSP, not RF hardware
  stacks. Software-only: gnuradio/gqrx/hackrf-tools, plus the audio
  DSP support rows (sox, librosa, pysox).
- **Data-row delivery is the same discipline, different shape:** these
  are `status: data` manifest rows — every fact (licence, source,
  update class) single-sourced like any tool — but the delivery is an
  opt-in derivation because of the size budget, and the opt-in never
  rides a default profile or a category toggle. `kailash-data.*` is the
  same mechanism as the wordlist packs; C-7 is simply the data-pack
  census category kept narrow by design (the spec's §3.6 D7 decision
  records exactly this: a data-pack toggle, NOT a tool-category of
  record — the category count stays 31).
- **Size budget honesty:** the ISO targets carry CI-enforced budgets
  (≤1.5/4/8/10 GB by target) and the budget check legs assert the
  heavies stay opt-in — texlive, gnuradio, the SDR/wordlist corpora.
  Opt in only where the work is: a headless DSP-training host can take
  the pack with no desktop in its closure.
- **Licensing note per row:** GNU Radio GPLv3, Gqrx GPLv3+, HackRF
  tools GPLv2+ — all GPL-family and established; the caveat that
  matters here is the one every data row carries: whatever corpora you
  CAPTURE with this pack are your content, your licence decision. The
  manifest row does not establish capture-content licences.
- **Neighbour discipline:** the same opt-in pattern covers every
  `kailash-data.*` pack — wordlists, texlive, the SDR six. The recipes'
  PENDING discipline applies here too: the pack PATH layout on a live
  system is the derivation's own record; the worked verification lands
  with the upkeep lane's host checks.
